title: Less wind for Lisbon?
standfirst: Late on Tuesday the press began to report that Storm Charles would pass further south, with less wind for Lisbon. At 07:16 on Wednesday IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange, with gusts up to 120 km/h still warned from 09:00. At 12:16 its communiqué no. 3 wrote that the storm had split in two and that its wind would be weaker than forecast on Tuesday; at 12:33 it cut Lisbon's red rain to 15:00 and its orange wind to 18:00, with gusts up to 90 km/h. This is what IPMA has written, what one of its meteorologists said aloud, what the headlines say, what the models in the data room show, and what IPMA's warnings for Lisbon say at the last read.

warnings_in_force.about: The official warnings a story about the storm states first, drawn as the front page draws them: for each kind of weather IPMA's newest message by the time it was sent (cap.json beside this file), saying what IPMA's open-data feed (this file) lists where the two differ; resolved when the page is built and read again in the reader's browser. Never a level of our own.

claims.text: IPMA named the storm CHARLES on Monday 9 November at 13:17, in communiqué no. 1, and said its path and strength carried "elevada incerteza".
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, communiqué no. 1

supports.note: No longer in IPMA's feed: kept from the record of the newsroom that read it at the time.

claims.text: Communiqué no. 2, edited on Tuesday at 17:07, put the centre's most likely path "entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro", a stretch of coast that has Lisbon inside it, with the strongest gusts "no bordo sul da depressão": 100 to 120 km/h, locally up to 140.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, communiqué no. 2

contains: a maior probabilidade será o centro da depressão passar entre Sines e o Cabo Carvoeiro
no bordo sul da depressão as rajadas serão da ordem dos 100 a 120 km/h, podendo ser localmente até 140 km/h
elevada incerteza na trajetória e intensidade

claims.text: Communiqué no. 3, edited on Wednesday at 12:16:26, is IPMA's first text on Charles since Tuesday. It says the depression passed north of Madeira and "se dividiu em dois núcleos de baixa pressão distintos", unlike the numerical models first had it, and that this means "uma diminuição do cavamento da depressão, e consequentemente da intensidade do vento, face à previsão do dia de ontem". It still has persistent, at times heavy rain, moving from south-west to north-east, and the wind strengthening in the South, with gusts of 70 to 90 km/h, up to 110 km/h on exposed coast and high ground; the warnings "foram ajustados".
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's communiqués feed

claims.text: IPMA's own hourly model for Lisbon has moved three times between our reads. On Tuesday evening, under an unchanged stamp, Wednesday's strongest mean wind went from 48.6 km/h at 18:00 to 23.4 km/h at 20:00. From the 08:45 read on Wednesday it was 40 km/h at 14:00, from the south (last read so at 19:29). At the 20:23 read, under the same stamp (07:56 Lisbon time), the same hour is 36 km/h, still from the south: the run was changed after its hour had passed. Measured at the airport at 14:00: 54 km/h, gusting 74.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: IPMA's automatic hourly forecast for Lisbon (a model's output, not a warning)

supports.note: The run as last read before it was replaced.
The run as last read before it was changed.

claims.text: MET Norway's forecast for Lisbon, at its update of 13:17 on Wednesday, has the strongest mean wind of the afternoon at 46.4 km/h at 14:00, from the south-south-west, and the lowest pressure, 988.8 hPa, in the same hour; then 39.2 km/h from the south-west at 15:00, turning west by 16:00 and north-west by 17:00 as the wind eases. At its update of 08:21 it had 55.1 km/h at 15:00. This block carries no gusts (it has updated since, about every two hours). Measured at the airport at 14:00: 54 km/h from the south, gusting 74, and 989 hPa, close to the model's hour (our comparison). The feed has since dropped the hours it covered.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: MET Norway, Locationforecast 2.0 (a second model, never merged with IPMA)

claims.text: Open-Meteo's forecast for the same point is far lower, and moves a little at most reads (its past hours too): between 09:00 and 21:00 its strongest mean wind is now 22.7 km/h, at 16:00 from the west-north-west, and its strongest gust 57.2 km/h, at 17:00 from the west-north-west; it has 10:00 at 20.1 km/h from the south, and 14:00 at 10.5 km/h gusting 50, from the south (at 15:23: 20.8 gusting 55.4, from the north-east).
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Open-Meteo, best match (a second model, never merged with IPMA)

claims.text: The airport's forecast, written by IPMA for pilots, held through the night and was then lowered. The one issued at 05:00 on Wednesday kept 30 knots gusting 45 (83 km/h) at times to 18:00. The amendment of 10:08 cut that to 20 knots gusting 35 (65 km/h) at times to 16:00, and the forecast issued at 11:00 repeats the cut: at times between 12:00 and 16:00, 20 knots gusting 35 (65 km/h), with a 30% chance of gusts of 55 knots (102 km/h) in thunderstorms in the same hours, and the wind turning west-north-west between 16:00 and 18:00. The airport measured 74 km/h at 14:00, above the 65 it had at times. The amendment of 14:36 has 23 knots gusting 38 (70 km/h) to 16:00, the wind becoming west-north-west by 18:00, at times gusting 27 knots (50 km/h) from 18:00 to 21:00; the thunderstorm group is gone. The forecast issued at 17:00, the first to cover all of Thursday, has west-north-west 24 km/h from 18:00, turning south-west by 02:00, showers at times, and gusts of 27 knots (50 km/h) at times from 10:00 to 18:00 on Thursday.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA, the TAF for Lisbon airport (a point forecast for pilots, not a public warning)

claims.text: So the three models in the data room do not agree with each other: the strongest mean wind for Lisbon on Wednesday is 40, 55.1 or 19.4 km/h, at 14:00, 15:00 or 10:00, depending on which is read. IPMA's and MET Norway's are now an hour apart on when, and 15 km/h apart on how strong. None of these is a gust at an exposed place, which is what the warning's 120 km/h measures.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: this desk, setting three files side by side

supports.note: The data room's own note: the airport's gusts and the warning's gusts "are not the same measure"; second models are kept one block per source, "never merged with IPMA".

claims.text: Inside the windows (they opened at 09:00 on Wednesday; the last closed at 18:00), the airport's nineteen reports from 09:00 to 18:00 fall in two parts. Until 13:30 the wind was 17 to 28 km/h, backing from south-south-east through east to east-north-east and then east again, with no gust reported, heavy rain from 10:30 and visibility down to 1.5 km at 13:00. Between 13:30 and 14:00 the wind turned from east to south and rose from 17 to 54 km/h, gusting 74 km/h (40 knots), with wind shear reported on runway 20 and the temperature up 2 °C; at 15:00 it was south-south-west 41 km/h gusting 61 km/h, the rain over and visibility above 10 km, wind shear still reported; at 15:30 and 16:00 south-south-west 37 and 39 km/h (gusting 61 at 15:30, no gust at 16:00), light rain and drizzle again and visibility 1.5 km. Then the wind turned: west 22 km/h at 16:30, west-north-west 20 km/h gusting 43 km/h at 17:00, and north-west 22 km/h at 17:30 and 24 km/h gusting 50 km/h at 18:00, no rain reported and visibility above 10 km. The pressure fell from 1001 to 989 hPa by 14:00 and held at 989 to 16:00, then rose: 990 hPa at 16:30, 991 at 17:00 and 17:30, 992 at 18:00. IPMA's newest station hour is the one labelled 17:00: no rain at the six stations that reported (Oeiras reported nothing) and mean winds of 11.9 to 25.2 km/h (Relógio the strongest), from the north-west and west; the hour labelled 16:00 had 0.0 to 1.2 mm (Oeiras the most) and mean winds of 13.0 to 29.9 km/h from the west at Oeiras, Amoreiras and Almada; the hour labelled 15:00 had 0.0 to 1.2 mm and up to 36.7 km/h, all from the south-west; the hour labelled 14:00 had 1.2 to 6.8 mm and up to 41.0 km/h at Oeiras, the strongest mean wind of the day, and the hour labelled 13:00 5.9 to 26.2 mm (Oeiras, the heaviest single hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations in the data room's record of the storm). The 74 km/h gust is below the gust warned for its hour (90 km/h, 110 in the most exposed places). The red rain ended at 15:00 as set. At 15:55:03 IPMA ended the orange wind at 15:56, two hours early (its message, in the data room's copy from the 16:22:55 read). So the wind window is over: in the airport's reports inside it, from 09:00 to 15:30, no gust reached the warned gust, the strongest 74 km/h at 14:00. The yellow rain ended at 18:00 as set, so every window this story was told against has closed. Left in force for Lisbon: the orange sea warning to 21:00, then yellow to 03:00 on Thursday (not an all-clear).
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's stations and the airport's METAR, as read

claims.text: The strongest gust in the airport's reports we hold is now 40 knots (74 km/h), from the south at 14:00 on Wednesday, inside the window; before it, the strongest was 36 knots (67 km/h), on Tuesday at 11:00. The gust warned for that hour is 90 km/h, 110 in the most exposed places, and the data room's list of airport gusts above the gust warned for their hour, kept from 05:00 on Wednesday, is still empty.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Lisbon airport's METAR (issued by IPMA, read through NOAA's Aviation Weather)

supports.note: A tripwire: the data room lists here every airport gust from Wed 05:00 above the gust warned for that hour. Empty at this read.

claims.text: After the warning was lowered the press reported it, and attributed more to IPMA than IPMA has written. Titles read at 09:39: TSF, "Previsões do IPMA melhoram: apenas Faro está sob aviso vermelho para vento"; RTP, "Depressão Charles divide-se em dois e enfraquece, mas a chuva vai manter-se forte". Every outlet read keeps the red rain, and the levels they give match IPMA's messages of 07:16:30. That the storm "splits in two and weakens" is the press reporting IPMA's spoken word: IPMA had then published no communiqué after no. 2 and no new message for Lisbon since 07:16. It wrote the split at 12:16, in communiqué no. 3 (c3), some two and a half hours after those titles were read.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: TSF and RTP (titles), as read by incident.weatherwatch@; not read at IPMA

claims.text: At 09:25 the meteorologist read the models again, and this supersedes the reading of 02:35: IPMA's hourly run of 07:56 and MET Norway's of 09:19 now both turn the wind through south and south-west to west, so the centre is read as passing close to Lisbon and just north of it between about 13:00 and 15:00, earlier than the 15:00 to 18:00 held before. On a drop in the wind around midday in both models, the analysis's words are: "a lull ~12:00-13:00 precedes the strongest wind; not the end". This is our analysis and not a forecast; IPMA's warnings are what stand: red rain to 18:00, orange wind to 21:00.
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: medium, on which side of Lisbon the centre passes
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

claims.text: On the press's "two centres", the meteorologist wrote at 09:50: IPMA had put nothing in writing about two centres (it did at 12:16, in communiqué no. 3: "dois núcleos de baixa pressão distintos"). Madeira airport's wind swung between 07:00 and 08:00 with its pressure lowest at 06:30; one centre could not pass Madeira then and reach Lisbon, 966 km away, by 13:00 to 15:00 without moving at 140 to 160 km/h. So Madeira's swing was most likely a separate feature: consistent with two centres, not proof of them. The test it sets for Lisbon: the airport's pressure bottoming near 988 to 992 hPa at about 14:00 to 15:00, with the wind turning through south-west.
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: medium (observations and distance; not IPMA in writing)
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

supports.expect: medium (observations and distance; not IPMA in writing)

claims.text: At 11:30 the meteorologist added, with low confidence: the airport's wind backing from south-south-east to east-south-east while the pressure falls hints that the centre may pass south of Lisbon, not just north of it as read at 09:25. The pressure minimum and the wind's turn between 13:00 and 16:00 will settle it. Radio Observador reported at 10:38 that the overnight reassessment moved the track further south, toward the Algarve; that is the press, not IPMA's written word. This is our analysis and not a forecast; IPMA's warnings are what stand.
claims.label: hypothesis

claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

claims.text: At 12:25 the meteorologist revised the reading again, now with medium confidence: the airport's wind backing to east-north-east while the pressure fell 4 hPa in an hour puts Lisbon on the storm's north side, so the centre is likely over or just south of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00, not just north of it as read at 09:25. Lisbon's strongest wind may come after the centre passes, from the north-west or west, and rain is now the main hazard. Its test: the wind turning through north to north-west would mean the centre passed south. Not borne out: the airport's wind went from south-south-west to west and west-north-west (16:30, 17:00), and the meteorologist's analysis 25 (high confidence) has the centre passing just north. This is our analysis and not a forecast; IPMA's warnings are what stand.
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: medium (the wind's backing and the pressure fall at one airport, and the models)
claims.said_by: incident.meteorologist@web-summit.dinis (analysis; not IPMA's words)

contains: centre now likely over or just south of Lisbon (medium)

claims.text: Our data scientist read the 51 forecasts of ECMWF's ensemble again at 21:52, on the newest run Open-Meteo held, made after the centre had passed: the low crosses the line off Lisbon (9.5° W) north of the city in 6% of them, near it in 53% and south of it in 41% (at 15:52: 24%, 47% and 29%; at 11:57: 10%, 41% and 49%), the middle of them still about 15:00; Lisbon's strongest model gust still has a median of 65 km/h (10% of forecasts below 53, 10% above 80). A run made after the event is closer to a model's reconstruction than a forecast; it does not settle which side the centre passed (h11, the meteorologist's reading, has it just north). These are shares of forecasts, not the chance of it happening. Our analysis of a model, not a forecast; IPMA's warnings are what stand.
claims.label: hypothesis
claims.confidence: medium for the north, near and south split; low for gust values at a point (the file's own words)
claims.said_by: incident.datascience@web-summit.dinis (analysis of ECMWF's ensemble via Open-Meteo)

claims.text: At 12:33:13 on Wednesday IPMA shortened Lisbon's warnings. Red rain now runs from 12:34 to 15:00 (it had run to 18:00), then yellow rain from 15:00 to 18:00. The orange wind warning runs from 12:34 to 18:00 (it had run to 21:00) and now reads "Rajadas até 90 km/h, podendo atingir 110 km/h nos locais mais expostos", where the message of 07:16:30 said gusts up to 120 km/h. No new message for the sea: its orange warning, 12:00 to 21:00, stands. The red rain ended at 15:00 as that message set it, and no newer message for Lisbon had been sent by the 15:23:13 read: yellow rain and the orange wind stood to 18:00, the orange sea to 21:00. At 15:55:03 IPMA ended the orange wind at 15:56 instead of 18:00 (the data room's copy of the messages holds it from the 16:22:55 read; first seen in MeteoAlarm's feed at 16:09, row s-1111T1609): Lisbon now has yellow rain to 18:00 and the orange sea to 21:00, then yellow sea to 03:00. Not an all-clear. IPMA's open-data feed caught up with the message of 12:33 at about 14:20, 1 hour 50 minutes later.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: IPMA's CAP messages, as carried by MeteoAlarm's feed

supports.expect: Rajadas até 90 km/h, podendo atingir 110 km/h nos locais mais expostos.

claims.text: At 14:25 the meteorologist revised the reading again, revising the one of 12:25: with the airport's wind turning from east to south and rising to 54 km/h gusting 74, wind shear, and the temperature up 2 °C while the pressure still fell, a warm sector is arriving, and the centre is now more likely to pass just north of Lisbon, as read at 09:25. On that reading Lisbon is now in the strongest-wind sector (south to south-west), turning west to north-west once the pressure rises; the airport forecast has the wind from 290 degrees from 16:00 to 18:00. The pressure minimum and the turn to the west will test it. At 15:25 (analysis 22), with the airport's pressure steady at 989 hPa for an hour and the wind south-south-west, the meteorologist wrote that the centre is passing just north now; the worst rain was 12:00 to 14:30 and the strongest wind from 14:00, turning west to north-west from 16:00 to 18:00 by the airport forecast. At about 17:24 (analysis 25, high confidence) it wrote that the centre passed just north, closest about 14:30 to 16:30; the airport's wind turned west by 16:30 and the pressure rose from 17:00. This is our analysis and not a forecast; IPMA's warnings are what stand.
claims.label: hypothesis

not_known.text: Whether IPMA will publish a communiqué no. 3, or change Lisbon's warnings again: the wind warning was lowered to orange at 07:16 on Wednesday; the red rain warning stands.
What Antena 1's 22:00 bulletin said, and who said it: it is audio and was not heard, so whether IPMA's word was first on RTP or on Observador is not settled.
What a second IPMA meteorologist is reported to have told Renascença: the page refused automated reads and is not in this story.
The time of Público's live entry: its headline was read at 00:29, its entry time was not.
Why IPMA's hourly model changed its values under the same stamp.

Our own captures of the press pages: the evidence section is not built yet, so a press claim here links to the timeline row or data file that holds it and then to the outlet, not yet to a dated capture with a hash.
How much wind Lisbon gets. That is for Wednesday's observations, from 12:00.

record.what: First telling, on the data read at 01:51:55 UTC: 26 sentences. Lisbon's red wind and red rain warnings stand; no communiqué no. 3; three models in the data room disagree; nothing observed yet tests it.

Checked against the read of 02:22:46 UTC. Nothing moved at IPMA: the same warnings for Lisbon, the communiqué still no. 2. Nothing moved in the three models. The airport's latest report is now 02:00 (wind from 200° at 5 knots, 1006 hPa), so the two sentences on the observations were retold.

The hypothesis layer retold from the meteorologist's re-weighing of 02:35 UTC (analysis.md 7b, row s-1111T0229), which followed this story's note that an input had moved. Before: "very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00, more likely just south", confidence medium; headline guidance "IPMA's forecasters expect the strongest winds south of Lisbon; Lisbon's red warnings stand". Now: which side of Lisbon the centre passes is unsettled (low); very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00 (medium); "'less wind for Lisbon' is not supported". Nothing changed at IPMA: the red warnings stand. Row supports now show our own capture first where the evidence section holds one.

Checked against the read of 02:38:08 UTC: nothing moved at IPMA or in the models. The two sentences on the observations no longer quote the airport's newest half-hourly report (it was 02:00: wind from 200° at 5 knots, 1006 hPa); they now say what holds until something measurable happens, with tripwires on the first station hour at 12:00 and on the first gust above the warned gust.

Checked against the read of 03:23:31 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2, the models unchanged. One sentence added from a new timeline row (s-1111T0328): RTP's 03:00 bulletin title puts the shift south under IPMA's name again; IPMA has still written nothing new. Three supports now name the 01:29 re-read by its time (the list of re-reads had grown).

Checked against the read of 04:23:17 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2. One model moved: Open-Meteo's strongest mean wind was 20.6 km/h (gust 52.6) at 14:00 from the north-east; it is now 18.7 km/h (gust 53.6) at 10:00 from the south-south-west. MET Norway's values and IPMA's hourly model are as before. The three still disagree.

Checked against the read of 05:22:49 UTC: IPMA's red wind and red rain for Lisbon unchanged, the communiqué still no. 2. A new airport forecast (issued 05:00): the 45-knot gust group now runs 09:00 to 18:00 (the 23:00 issue, which this story quoted as "weaker at 23:00 than at 17:00", ended it at 16:00); the 30% chance of 58-knot gusts is kept. MET Norway re-stamped its run with the same values.

Checked against the read of 06:25:17 UTC: IPMA's red rain (09:00 to 18:00) and red wind (12:00 to 21:00) for Lisbon unchanged. Open-Meteo's values moved. Before: strongest mean 18.7 km/h and strongest gust 53.6 km/h, both at 10:00, from the south-south-west; 16.1 km/h at 14:00. Now: 19.4 km/h at 10:00 and 50 km/h at 11:00, from the south; 17.6 km/h at 14:00.

The top of the story changed. Before: IPMA had sent no message that lowered, shortened or lifted a Lisbon warning; red wind 12:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h and 140 in the most exposed places. Now: at 07:16:30 on Wednesday IPMA lowered the wind warning to orange, 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h (row s-1111T0738); red rain unchanged; IPMA's open-data feed still showed red wind at 07:38; the meteorologist's reading of 07:45 added. Supports for the red wind warning now point at the kept CAP message, since the replaced warning leaves the feed.

The box at the top is now drawn from both of IPMA's channels, as the front page draws it: the newest message for each kind of weather, and what the open-data feed still lists where the two differ (before, it was drawn from the open data alone and showed red wind after IPMA's 07:16 message had lowered it to orange). The supports for Lisbon's red rain warning (09:00 to 18:00) now point at IPMA's kept message (PO-10-6290, sent 10 Nov 21:23) rather than the open-data list, which drops a warning when it ends; no sentence changed.

Retold on the read of 08:45:09 UTC. Before: IPMA's open-data feed still showed red wind (07:38). Now: the feed has the orange warning, 66 to 88 minutes after the message (row s-1111T0844). Before: IPMA's hourly model had Wednesday's strongest mean wind at 23.4 km/h at 20:00; now 40 km/h at 14:00, from the south. Before: MET Norway 58.3 km/h and 987.7 hPa at 15:00; now 55.1 km/h and 988.8 hPa at 15:00. The comparison of the three models follows. The warning windows open at 09:00; nothing measured inside them is in this telling.

Retold on the read of 09:22:47 UTC, the first after the windows opened at 09:00. Before, o1 said: "Nothing measured yet can test any of this: the orange wind warning and the red rain warning both begin at 09:00 on Wednesday, and the observations we hold end before it." Now it gives the one measurement held from inside the windows (the airport at 09:00: 20 km/h, no gust reported) and says the station hours end at 08:00. o2 stands: no airport gust above the warned gust is listed.

Added from rows s-1111T0922, s-1111T0939 and s-1111T0941: the press on the lowered warning and "two centres" (c21, evidence); the meteorologist's reading of 09:25, which supersedes that of 02:35 (h6: just north of Lisbon, about 13:00 to 15:00, medium confidence; before, h1 and h4 had the side unsettled and 15:00 to 18:00); and its reading of "two centres" (h7). h1 to h5 are kept as what was held when.

Retold on the read of 10:22:42 UTC. Before: o1 said: "The windows opened at 09:00 on Wednesday (orange for wind, red for rain), and one measurement from inside them is in the data room: the airport's 09:00 report, south-south-east 20 km/h with no gust reported, rain and mist, 1001 hPa. That is the same wind as at 08:00 and 08:30. IPMA's station hours we hold end at the one labelled 08:00, before the windows. One report at the opening minute cannot test any of this." c17 said: "The airport's forecast, written by IPMA for pilots, has not eased since: the one issued at 05:00 on Wednesday keeps 30 knots gusting 45 (83 km/h) at times, now from 09:00 to 18:00 (the 23:00 issue ended that at 16:00), with a 30% chance of gusts of 58 knots (107 km/h) in thunderstorms between 10:00 and 18:00." c16 said: "Open-Meteo's forecast for the same point is far lower, and moved again between reads: its strongest mean wind is now 19.4 km/h, at 10:00, and its strongest gust 50 km/h, at 11:00, both from the south. At 14:00 it has 17.6 km/h from the north-east." Now: o1 gives the airport's three reports inside the windows and the station hour labelled 09:00; c17 gives the airport forecast amended at 10:08 (lowered: 65 km/h at times to 16:00, was 83 km/h to 18:00; row s-1111T1028); c16 gives Open-Meteo's figures as they now stand.

On the 11:26:40 read. o1 retold: before, the airport's three reports to 10:00 and the station hour labelled 09:00 (3.0 to 6.5 mm at six stations, which might lie before the windows); now five reports to 11:00 (17 to 22 km/h, backing to east-south-east, no gust, heavy rain, 998 hPa) and the hour labelled 10:00, inside the windows on either reading (3.8 to 5.9 mm at seven stations). Tripwire now the airport's 12:00 report. c17 retold: the 11:00 TAF repeats the 10:08 cut, for 12:00 to 16:00, the wind turning west-north-west 16:00 to 18:00 (before: the 10:08 amendment, turning west 18:00 to 20:00). h8 added (row s-1111T1128b, low confidence: the centre may pass south of Lisbon); h6 stands as what was held at 09:25.

On the 12:23:12 read. o1 retold: before, five airport reports to 11:00 (17 to 22 km/h, backing to east-south-east, 998 hPa) and the station hour labelled 10:00 (3.8 to 5.9 mm at seven stations, strongest mean wind 18.4 km/h at Barreiro); now seven reports to 12:00 (17 to 28 km/h, backing to east and east-north-east, no gust, 994 hPa) and the hour labelled 11:00, the wettest inside the windows so far (11.5 to 17.9 mm at six stations, Oeiras the most; strongest mean wind 23.8 km/h at Oeiras). Tripwire now the airport's 13:00 report. c16 retold: before, Open-Meteo's strongest mean wind 18.9 km/h at 10:00 and gust 50.8 km/h at 11:00, both from the south-south-west, and 16.7 km/h at 14:00; now its strongest mean wind 20.8 km/h and gust 55.4 km/h, both at 14:00 from the north-east.

On the 12:23:12 read. h9 added: the meteorologist's 12:25 reading (medium: the centre likely over or just south of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00; the strongest wind may come after, from the north-west or west; rain the main hazard), which revises h6 (09:25, just north) and raises h8 (11:30, low). h10 added: the ensemble's shares (north 10%, near 41%, south 49%, about 15:00), a model read as analysis.

On the 12:49:59 read. c3 retold: before, "IPMA has published no communiqué no. 3: at the last read, no. 2 is still the newest text on Charles in its feed."; now communiqué no. 3 (12:16:26): two centres, less deepening and so less wind than forecast on Tuesday, gusts 70 to 90 km/h in the South. c22 added: the 12:33:13 messages cut Lisbon's red rain to 15:00 (then yellow to 18:00) and its orange wind to 18:00, gusts up to 90 km/h, 110 exposed (was 120, to 21:00). o1 retold: before, seven airport reports to 12:00 (to 994 hPa) and the station hour labelled 11:00 (11.5 to 17.9 mm), against gusts up to 120 km/h warned to 21:00; now eight reports to 12:30 (still no gust, 992 hPa) and the hour labelled 12:00 (8.7 to 18.7 mm at seven stations, Relógio the most; strongest mean wind 29.5 km/h at Oeiras), against the warning as cut at 12:33 (gusts up to 90 km/h, 110 exposed, to 18:00; red rain to 15:00). Tripwire now the airport's 13:00 report. c21 and h7: "IPMA has put nothing in writing" was true when written and is now past; both say it wrote the split at 12:16. Standfirst brought to 12:33.

On the 13:24:33 read. o1 retold: before, eight airport reports to 12:30 (992 hPa); now nine to 13:00: east 20 km/h, no gust, visibility 1.5 km, 991 hPa, 8 hPa down since 10:00 and still falling. The station hour is still the one labelled 12:00. Tripwire now the airport's 14:00 report.

On the 14:23:47 read. o1 retold: before, nine airport reports to 13:00 (east 20 km/h, no gust, 991 hPa) and the station hour labelled 12:00 (8.7 to 18.7 mm, Relógio the most); now eleven to 14:00, with the turn to south 54 km/h gusting 74 km/h, wind shear, 989 hPa still falling, and the hour labelled 13:00 (5.9 to 26.2 mm, Oeiras the most, the heaviest hour at IPMA's Lisbon stations in our record). o2 retold: the strongest airport gust was 67 km/h on Tuesday 11:00, now 74 km/h at 14:00 Wednesday, below the warned 90/110. c15 retold: MET Norway's 08:21 update had 55.1 km/h at 15:00; its 13:17 update has 46.4 km/h at 14:00. h3's support moved to the 13:17 update (17:00 from 303.7 degrees, was 274.9); its text stands. h11 added: the meteorologist's 14:25 reading (analysis 21), centre more likely just north, revising h9.

On the 15:23:13 read. c22: the red rain ended at 15:00 as set (before: the open-data feed had not caught up at 12:49:59; now: it caught up about 14:20, no newer message for Lisbon). o1 retold: before, eleven airport reports to 14:00 and the station hour labelled 13:00; now thirteen to 15:00 (south-south-west 41 km/h gusting 61, 989 hPa steady) and the hour labelled 14:00 (rain down to 1.2 to 6.8 mm, mean wind up to 41.0 km/h at Oeiras). h10 retold: ensemble shares north/near/south were 10/41/49%, now 24/47/29% (14:52 read). h11 adds analysis 22 (15:25: the centre passing just north now).

h10 retold on incident.datascience@'s 15:52:55 read of the ensemble: Lisbon's strongest model gust, before median 69.1 km/h (p10 55.4, p90 85); now 64.8 (52.9, 79.9). The north, near and south shares are unchanged (24/47/29).

IPMA's batch of 15:55:03 (row s-1111T1609). c22: before, "yellow rain and the orange wind stand to 18:00"; now the orange wind ended at 15:56, yellow rain to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00 then yellow to 03:00. o1: before, "the orange wind stand[s] to 18:00, so the wind window is not over"; now the wind window closed at 15:56, no gust above the warned gust in the reports read to 15:00. Supports from cap.json to follow once the data room's copy holds the batch.

On the 16:22:55 read. o1: before, thirteen airport reports to 15:00 and the station hour labelled 14:00, the wind window open; now fifteen to 16:00 (37 and 39 km/h, 989 hPa, drizzle) and the hour labelled 15:00 (rain 0.0 to 1.2 mm, mean wind 17.6 to 36.7 km/h), and the wind window over at 15:56 with no gust reaching the warned gust (IPMA's message PO-01-1945, now in the data room's copy). c22: the same message as support. c15: MET Norway's feed dropped the hours before 16:00 (same 13:17 update); the 14:00 values kept as read, beside the airport's 14:00 report. c16: Open-Meteo moved (strongest mean 20.8 at 14:00 -> 20.1 at 10:00; gust 55.4 at 14:00 -> 52.2 at 17:00). c17: the airport forecast amended at 14:36 (before: the 11:00 issue was the newest).
o1: rows s-1111T1611 and s-1111T1624 added as supports; text unchanged.

On the 17:23:17 read. o1: before, to the airport's 16:00 and the station hour 15:00; now to 17:00 (the wind turned west and west-north-west, 991 hPa rising) and the hour labelled 16:00. c17: the forecast of 17:00 for Thursday (before: the 14:36 amendment was newest). c15: MET Norway updated at 17:20. h11: analysis 25 (centre passed just north, closest 14:30 to 16:30). h9: before, its test open; now not borne out.

On the 18:23:17 read. o1: before, to the airport's 17:00 and the station hour 16:00, yellow rain standing to 18:00; now to 18:00 (north-west 24 km/h gusting 50, 992 hPa rising) and the hour labelled 17:00 (no rain), and closed: the yellow rain ended at 18:00 as set, every window the story was told against is over; only the sea warnings remain. c16: Open-Meteo revised its past hours (strongest gust 57.2 km/h at 17:00, was 52.2; strongest mean 22.7 at 16:00, was 20.1 at 10:00). h3: support on MET Norway's 17:00 removed (its feed keeps no past hours; its note said: the update of 13:17 had the wind from the north-west at 17:00, 303.7 degrees; the update of 08:21 274.9, the run of 01:19 283.1).
c15: the pin on MET Norway's update time removed (it updates about every two hours; the sentence is the 13:17 update as read, and the feed keeps no past hours). No sentence retold.

c14: before, IPMA's hourly model had Wednesday's strongest mean wind at 40 km/h at 14:00 (from the 08:45 read to the 19:29 read); now 36 km/h at the same hour under the same stamp (07:56 Lisbon time), changed after the hour had passed.

h10: before, the ensemble's shares as read at 15:52 (north 24%, near 47%, south 29%); now the 21:52 read of the newest run, made after the centre passed: north 6%, near 53%, south 41%; median crossing (15:00) and Lisbon's gust spread (53/65/80 km/h) unchanged. The sentence says a run made after the event does not settle which side the centre passed.
